newsitem.title: USA: US winter wheat reaches pre-frost output line-USDA.
newsitem.headline: US winter wheat reaches pre-frost output line-USDA.

text.p: The U.S. winter wheat crop has rebounded from a springtime frost and will produce as much wheat as if there was no damage, two USDA officials said Friday.

The officials said ideal growing weather allowed plants to recover and would allow farmers to harvest 800,000 acres that originally were expected to be abandoned. USDA pegged the crop at 1.78 billion bushels, up 11 percent from one month ago.
"Yes, we are back," said Fred Vogel, director of the estimates division of the National Agricultural Statistics Service.
Vogel and Bill Dowdy, NASS director for field crops, told reporters that high head counts and heavy head weights made up for the effect of the freeze.
In Kansas and Missouri, yields were forecast to be eight bushels an acre higher than estimated last month. Kansas had a record head count.
Vogel described the growing season after the frost as "nature at its best" for wheat -- cool and sunny but not so hot as to curb the crop's potential.
